targets.authors: Malhotra, N. K., Kim, S. S., & Agarwal, J.
targets.title: Internet users’ information privacy concerns (IUIPC): The construct, the scale, and a causal model.
targets.evidence_quote: The main aim of the present study was to verify the applicability of the IUIPC model of Malhotra et al. (2004) in Japan, especially focusing on the comparison to the original USA sample as well as on changes due to differences in time when conducting the studies (difference of eleven years).
targets.outcome_quote: Our results indicate that the second-order IUIPC construct, measured reflectively through the constructs awareness, collection, and control, is reliable and valid. Furthermore, three out of the five structural paths of the IUIPC model were confirmed for our Japanese sample. In contrast to the original study, the impact of IUIPC on trusting beliefs, as well as that of trusting beliefs on risk beliefs was negligible.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The construct and three structural paths were confirmed; authors explicitly contrast two negligible paths against the original.

targets.title: Examining the influence of demographic factors on internet users’ information privacy concerns.
targets.evidence_quote: Our replication of the analysis by Zukowski and Brown (2007), regarding covariate effects, only confirmed the effects of gender on the privacy concerns in Japan.
targets.outcome_quote: Even though the correlation of IUIPC with age is significant, we consider it negligible in magnitude (0.113). Zukowski and Brown again obtain a different result from what we observed in Japan by accepting their hypothesis of an effect of age. Similarly, our correlation of IUIPC with the education and personal income levels yields negligible values of 0.03, and -0.05 respectively. Zukowski and Brown, however, do identify an effect of education, but also reject the effect of income.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly call the covariate analysis a replication. Age and education differ, while absence of income effect agrees; gender also differs. Earlier IUIPC replications cited solely for context are not targets.

reasoning: Full 18-page article from author website; title, seven authors, DOI, and references verified. New Japanese sample tests the IUIPC model and explicitly replicates a separate demographic analysis.
